description: Post-hoc valence control analysis to test if anger bias is explained by valence alone

chi_square_within_negative.interpretation: Anger is over-predicted even within negative valence category

cross_valence_comparison.interpretation: Anger bias is stronger for negative valence gold labels, but present for positive too

key_finding: The anger bias is NOT explained by valence alone. Within the negative valence category, when sadness/fear/disgust are misclassified to another negative emotion, anger receives 55.6% of misclassifications vs 33.3% expected under uniform distribution (chi-square p<0.001). This indicates a specific 'anger default' beyond mere valence detection.
paper_text: To test whether the anger bias simply reflects valence detection, we analyzed misclassifications within valence categories. For negative-valence gold labels (sadness, fear, disgust), if misclassified to another negative emotion, anger received 55.6% of predictions versus 33.3% expected under uniform distribution (chi-square(1) = 161.4, p < 0.001). This confirms anger over-prediction is not explained by valence alone---models show a specific 'anger default' even when other negative emotions would be valence-appropriate.
